title: SDK experimental telemetry hypothesis journal (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Quick journal/working doc to outline telemetry experiments we want to embed in SDK quickstarts and sample apps. Goal: collect lightweight, privacy-safe signals that help us iterate on first-run friction without overwhelming the user or our billing. This is intentionally small scope: prototype event surface + short rollout plan + acceptance metrics.

Context / motivation
---
- We ship many quickstarts (JS, Python, Go, Docker) but have poor visibility into which steps users hit, where they drop, and which examples lead to long-term adoption.
- Current telemetry is either too coarse (account-level usage) or too heavy (full onboarding analytics). Need a middle path: short-lived, opt-out friendly telemetry for onboarding flow improvements.
- This doc focuses on the SDK-level instrumentation we add to sample apps / quickstarts (not runtime product telemetry for hosted inference).

Core hypotheses
---
1) Minimal event surface (5–7 events) is sufficient to identify the top 3 onboarding failure modes within 2 weeks for a cohort of 200 testers.
2) Short, client-side latency metrics + error-context (sdk_init, api_key_format_error, sample_request_failure) will surface common setup bugs (misconfigured env var, mismatched API version) faster than support tickets.
3) Exposing an opt-in telemetry banner in quickstarts increases opt-in rate to >=25% in internal beta and gives actionable signals without privacy concerns.

Signals to capture (proposed)
---
Event naming pattern: rd_sdk_quickstart.<phase> (namespace avoids collisions)
- rd_sdk_quickstart.started -> fired when user runs the quickstart script or hits the sample app main route (attach language/runtime, quickstart_id)
- rd_sdk_quickstart.auth_attempt -> on first client attempt to call Redwood API (attach auth_method: env/apiKey/profile)
- rd_sdk_quickstart.auth_error -> capture non-sensitive error code (401/403/invalid_format) + error_hint (short string)
- rd_sdk_quickstart.first_api_success -> completed first successful generate/embed call (token_count_bucket, latency_ms_bucket)
- rd_sdk_quickstart.manual_steps_skipped -> user skipped optional steps (notebook, telemetry opt-in) — helps assess friction
- rd_sdk_quickstart.telemetry_opt_in -> boolean event when user chooses to opt-in
- rd_sdk_quickstart.uninstalled -> if quickstart cleans up or user presses stop (helps compute churn)

Minimal payload fields (privacy-first)
---
- quickstart_id (string) e.g., js-basic-chat-v2
- runtime (string) e.g., node16, python3.11
- sdk_version (string) e.g., 0.9.1
- event (string) e.g., started
- status_code_bucket (string) e.g., 4xx, 5xx (no full body)
- latency_bucket (string) e.g., <100ms, 100-500ms, 500-1000ms, >1s
- anonymized_country (string) optional, coarse (continent-level)
- opt_in (yes/no) only for opt-in event
- error_hint (string) short tag: MALFORMED_KEY, NETWORK, RATE_LIMIT

We must not capture: API keys, emails, user content, full traces, or prompt text. The quickstart code will scrub any user-provided content before emitting.

Instrumentation strategies (per language)
---
- JS quickstarts: instrument in the sample app wrapper (quickstart-run.js). On start, present a small console prompt asking to opt-in, default: not opted. If opted, write a single-shot event to our ingestion endpoint using fetch with an SDK token (server-side proxy in sample app if hosted).
- Python: same pattern via quickstart_cli.py; if user runs --interactive, show opt-in. Avoid blocking startup; send event asynchronously.
- Dockerized examples: telemetry disabled by default; include a README step to enable via env var.

Telemetry ingestion & storage plan
---
- Temporary ingestion endpoint: telemetry-dev.redwood.ai/quickstart_v1 -> accepts JSON POST of the minimal payload.
- Store raw events in a low-retention table (7 days) to allow debugging. Aggregated metrics (counts per quickstart_id, error buckets, latency buckets, opt-in rates) pushed to our analytics store (BigQuery) with 90-day retention by default.
- Access control: only eng-developer-experience + product-devexp have read access to the dev dataset.

Acceptance metrics (how we know it works)
---
Primary metrics (first 2 weeks after rollout to internal beta):
- Opt-in rate among internal participants >= 25%
- For active quickstarts (>=50 starts), at least one actionable error pattern discovered (e.g., >10% auth_error MALFORMED_KEY)
- Time to insight: median time from event to dashboard update < 3 hours (we can tune ingestion pipeline)

Secondary metrics:
- Fraction of users who complete first_api_success >= 40% (baseline unknown)
- Reduction in support threads about quickstart setup by 20% after fixes shipped (measured by JIRA tag match)

Quickstart experiment roadmap (milestones)
---
- Week 0 (prototype): implement minimal JS + Python instrumentation in internal samples. Bake opt-in prompt. Manual event POST to telemetry-dev endpoint. (Owners: Maya + Arjun)
- Week 1 (beta): invite internal SEs + 3 external friendly customers (solicit via slack #beta-hackers). Collect events, validate privacy checks. (Owners: Maya, S. Martinez)
- Week 2 (analyze): run simple aggregation queries, identify top 3 failure patterns. Paper-propose fixes for docs and code samples.
- Week 3 (iterate): ship doc fixes + example changes, measure change in subsequent cohort.

Quickstart UX / copy sketches
---
- Console prompt (JS):
  "Help us improve the Redwood quickstart experience — send anonymous setup telemetry? (Y/n)"
- Web banner (sample app): small dismissible banner "Share anonymous setup metrics to help us improve guides" with link to privacy note. Default not checked.

Data privacy & compliance notes (must include before any rollout)
---
- Default must be opt-out (no passive collection). Explicit opt-in for quickstarts that run on user machines. For sample apps on our hosted pages, only coarse aggregate metrics allowed.
- We will publish a short privacy note in the quickstart README: what we collect, why, retention, how to opt-out, and contact support.
- No PII. No prompt text. No API keys. Any mis-identified sensitive info must be purged.

Open questions / risks
---
- Opt-in friction: will opt-in be low? Consider small incentive (badge, early access) for beta testers.
- In Docker examples users expect zero prompts — how to balance opt-in and low-friction?
- Customers running quickstarts in enterprise environments may object to any outgoing telemetry; need clear env var to disable and simple docs explaining how to run offline.
- Ingestion security: currently prototype uses a token in code samples — must rotate and hide in real world.

Immediate next actions (TODOs)
---

- [ ] Add opt-in banner copy + README note — Maya — due 2025-02-12
- [ ] Create telemetry-dev ingestion endpoint + minimal schema validation — infra ping: @Liam — due 2025-02-13
- [ ] Draft short privacy FAQ and doc snippet — Sofia — due 2025-02-12
- [ ] Plan internal beta cohort and Slack invite template — Maya — due 2025-02-16

Notes to self
---
- Keep event schema intentionally tiny; it's easier to expand later than to retract.
- Lean on existing analytics infra where possible (avoid building heavy pipelines).
- Prepare a short demo for next Tuesday sync showing raw events for one quickstart run.

References
---
- Existing quickstarts: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples
- Prior telemetry thread: slack://channel/devexp-telemetry (see thread pinned)
- Related JIRA: DEVEXP-209 (tracking quickstart onboarding work)

End of draft journal entry — will update after prototype data lands.
